speaker_role: current Harvard undergraduate (junior) speaking for the student Undergraduate Admissions Council; not an admissions officer
key_insights: The main essay can cover any topic within the word limit, so decide which story or trait you want the admissions office to see.
A useful test for a topic is whether writing about it makes you happy and proud.
Avoid the school-style five-paragraph structure; use free-form tools such as word webs or dumping every idea on paper.
Expect bad early drafts; published sample essays did not begin polished.
Keep the voice authentic and have a parent, teacher, sibling or friend give honest feedback, but submit your own work.
Scrapping a first draft entirely is fine.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker cites the Common App essay limit as 650 words.
reliability_notes: Speaker is a student, not an officer, so claims reflect personal experience; generic.
